findings.title: Real-git fixture tests are sent to test files that fake git and the filesystem
findings.description:
Tasks 12, 16, 18, 21, 23 and 24 say to use the Task 9 real temp-repo fixture inside existing test files. Each of those files fakes, for the whole file, the very modules the fixture needs to be real:
- `GuideDetector.test.ts` fakes `fs` and `gitExec` (lines 7, 12).
- `SubmoduleStrategy.test.ts` fakes `fs` and `gitExec` (lines 5, 10).
- `GuideManager.test.ts` fakes `fs`, `gitExec`, `GuideDetector` and all three strategies (lines 7–48).
- `build.test.ts`, `guides.test.ts`, `contextTools.test.ts` and `guideTools.test.ts` each fake `@context-forge/core/node`.

Vitest applies `vi.mock` to the whole file, so a fixture test added there never runs real git. It either fails or passes against the fakes, which gives false confidence. The context note "`SubmoduleStrategy.test.ts` is the place to look for an existing real-git temp-repo pattern" is also wrong: that file uses fakes only (line 72 checks fake calls).

Fix: state that the fixture-based tests go in new files with no fakes (for example `GuideDetector.checkout.test.ts`, `ensureCheckout.integration.test.ts`, `build.autoinit.test.ts`). Correct the note in the Context section.

findings.title: Task 9's fixture needs `protocol.file.allow`, and the CLI and MCP packages can't easily import it
findings.description:
**Git setting:** the fixture adds a local bare repo as a submodule, and later tasks run `git submodule update --init` against it. Git 2.38.1 and later block the `file` transport for submodules by default, so both `submodule add` and `SubmoduleStrategy.init()` fail in the fixture. The task should say to set `protocol.file.allow=always` for the test process (for example with `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`/`GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0`/`GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0`) so that the real `gitExec` calls also pick it up.

**Location:** the helper goes under `packages/core/tests/guides/helpers/`, but Tasks 21 and 23 use it from `packages/cli/tests` and `packages/mcp-server/tests`. Importing another package's test folder is outside the published package exports and may sit outside the tsconfig `rootDir`. Either name a shared location both packages can import, or say explicitly that the import goes by relative path and that both packages' test configs allow it.

findings.title: Task 11 throws from `detect()` itself, which goes beyond the design and breaks existing tests
findings.description:
In the design's Data Flow, `'error'` → throw happens inside `ensureCheckout()`. Task 11 instead makes `detect()` throw whenever `checkSyncStatus()` returns `'error'`. `detect()` is called by `cf guides info`, `guide_status`, `setup-ide` and `install()`, so each of these would now fail when `git submodule status` fails.

The existing fake-based submodule tests at `GuideDetector.test.ts:68-112` will start calling `checkSyncStatus()` through the fake `gitExec`. Unless those fakes are given a status response, they will get `'error'` and throw. Neither Task 11 nor Task 12 says to update them.

Fix: name the existing tests to update in Task 12. Also either confirm that `detect()` throwing is intended (and note how `cf guides info` behaves when git is unavailable) or follow the design and throw in `ensureCheckout()`.

findings.title: Task 15 contradicts itself on who sets the auto-init timeout, and no test checks it
findings.description:
Task 15 declares `init(operationPath: string)` and says it runs with `{ timeoutMs: GUIDE_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS }`. The next step says to "pass the timeout as an `init()` option" so that `sync()` stays unbounded. Task 17 never says `ensureCheckout()` passes the timeout.

Read literally, either `sync()` becomes bounded or auto-init stays unbounded, and either way D10 is broken. No test in Tasks 16 or 18 checks that the auto-init path sets `timeoutMs` or that `sync()` does not.

Fix: pick one signature, for example `init(operationPath, opts?: { timeoutMs?: number })`. Say that `ensureCheckout()` passes `GUIDE_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS` and `sync()` passes nothing. Add one test that checks the `gitExec` options for each caller.

findings.title: `cf init --strategy` ignores the no-flag case, and the alias warning is written in several places
findings.description:
**No-flag case:** Task 26 passes `normalizeGuideMethod(opts.strategy)` unconditionally. Task 2 requires empty input to throw. Plain `cf init` with no `--strategy` would therefore throw, or `undefined` reaches a function typed `string`. The step should normalize only when the flag is given; otherwise `guidesInstallAction` should resolve the strategy from config. Task 27 should add a no-flag case. Task 7 has the same gap for `cf guides install` without `--strategy`.

**Where the error ends up:** `init.ts:117-127` catches all install errors and turns them into a warning. If normalization happens inside that `try`, `--strategy bogus` exits 0 after the project is already registered (lines 103–108). Task 27's "fails with the valid-values message before any install" needs to say this check runs before project registration and that the command exits non-zero.

**Repeated code:** the stderr deprecation line is written in Task 7 (flag), Task 7 (config path) and Task 26. Move the normalize-and-warn step into `guidesInstallAction` so it accepts a raw string, and have `init.ts` pass the raw flag through. That leaves one place that formats the message (CLAUDE.md DRY rule).

findings.title: Two functional success criteria are only tested in core, not where the user would see them
findings.description:
- **"A project whose shared config has `guide.git_strategy: manual` installs as tarball with the same warning."** Task 6 only checks that core reports the alias. Task 8 tests only the `--strategy manual` flag. The warning that `guidesInstallAction` prints for the config path (Task 7, second step) has no test. Add a `guides.test.ts` case where the fake manager reports a config-sourced alias, and check that the message goes to stderr.
- **"A malformed shared config file makes `cf guides install` fail with the config error."** Task 6(c) uses a fake `ConfigManager.get()` that throws. Per the CLAUDE.md parser rule (test against real input), add one case using a real malformed config file in a temp directory, so the actual parse error is shown to propagate.

findings.title: D3 says to grep the MCP server for call sites, but Task 22 doesn't
findings.description:
D3 requires grepping `createContextPipeline`, `resolvePromptFilePath` and `GUIDE_RELATIVE_PATH` in both `packages/cli/src` and `packages/mcp-server/src`. Task 20 greps only the CLI. Task 22 names two line numbers but not how many tools they cover. It is unclear whether `prompt_list`, `prompt_get` and `context_build` are all covered, and Task 23 tests only `context_build`.

Add the MCP grep to Task 22, with the same "list covered call sites" success criterion as Task 20. Add one `prompt_get` case in Task 23.

findings.title: Commit markers are written inside checkbox items
findings.description: Commits are given as "Commit: …" text inside success-criteria checkboxes rather than as plain `**Commit**:` lines. The spacing is right: there are 14 commit points across 32 tasks, each after a test task passes. Only the format is off, and it may confuse task-checker. Also, Task 20 says to list call sites "in the commit body", but the commit happens at Task 21.

findings.title: Some small tasks could be merged
findings.description: Task 1 deliberately leaves core failing typecheck until Task 3. Merging Tasks 1 and 3 gives one task that compiles. Task 10, which only adds types, could go into Task 11. These are optional; the overall size suits a slice that covers three issues.

findings.title: Task 31 names the version before the release decision
findings.description: The CHANGELOG step writes "Unreleased (0.14.0)", but Task 32 and the design both leave the version to the PM at release time. Use a plain "Unreleased" heading.

findings.title: Success criteria coverage and sequencing
findings.description:
Every functional and technical criterion maps to a task:
- Auto-init and JSON output: Tasks 17–21.
- `cf guides info` checkout state: Task 24.
- Out-of-sync warning: Tasks 17, 18 and 21.
- Alias for the flag and config: Tasks 5–8.
- `cf init --strategy`: Tasks 26–27.
- Help text: Tasks 25–27.
- Managed notice and README: Tasks 28–30.
- Malformed config: Tasks 5–6.
- Greps: Tasks 3, 5 and 32.
- CHANGELOG and DEVLOG: Task 31.

There is no scope creep, and the task order follows the design's Implementation Notes with no circular dependencies.
